SEBI] However, the bench of Presiding Officer PS Dinesh Kumar and Technical Members Meera Swarup and Dheeraj Bhatnagar refused to otherwise interfere with the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s (SEBI) July 31 order barring Zee from accessing securities market for two months. This order would mean that Zee and its chief executive officer Punit Goenka can go ahead with the plan to issue fully convertible warrants to the promoter-group entity on a preferential basis for a ₹3,143-crore fundraise. This relief is subject to both Zee and Goenka depositing the full penalty mandated by SEBI within one week. The deadline for issuing warrants, which was expiring today, was extended by SAT by one week. The market-access ban imposed by SEBI will remain active barring this specific relief from SAT. items.title: Brand protection in the era of social commerce
items.summary: The rapid growth of social commerce has fundamentally altered how businesses build brands, engage consumers, and generate revenue. Social media platforms are no longer limited to communication and entertainment. They have evolved into sophisticated commercial ecosystems where businesses promote products, interact with consumers, complete transactions, and cultivate long term customer relationships. Platforms offering live shopping, influencer collaborations, short video marketing, and integrated purchasing features have transformed the commercial landscape across India. This evolution has created significant opportunities for businesses of every size. Startups, established enterprises, and independent entrepreneurs now reach national and international audiences without maintaining extensive physical retail infrastructure. Brand visibility has become easier to achieve than at any previous time. However, increased visibility has also expanded the scope of trademark misuse, counterfeit activity, impersonation, deceptive advertising, and unauthorised commercial exploitation. items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 13, urging the Union government to permanently freeze the Lok Sabha’s strength at 543 and retain the existing distribution of seats among states and Union Territories. In his letter, the Chief Minister pointed out the resolution adopted by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on August 12, which called for constitutional amendments to preserve the existing level of representation for states. “The existing number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to the states should be made permanent at the current level. Current distribution of seats among the states must be maintained. I kindly request you to consider the resolution passed by Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and bring necessary Constitutional amendments in this regard,” Vijay said in his letter. The Assembly resolution also sought the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha without changing the existing strength of 543.
